title: Safety Recovery in Reasoning Models Is Only a Few Early Steering Steps Away
claim: Monitoring a reasoning trace and injecting a corrective signal early restores safety lost to reasoning training, without hurting capability.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right; (a) pipeline with threshold, (b) grouped bar chart
description: Two panels. Panel (a) shows a red-outlined flow, Adversarial Query → robot icon (Reasoning MLRM) → Unsafe Reasoning → Unsafe Response, connected by red arrows. A blue arrow leads from the robot into a light-blue box labeled 'SafeThink: Targeted Safety Steering'. Inside, generation steps 1–2 are red documents that fall below a dotted 'Safety Threshold' line. Lightning-bolt 'safety steering token' icons push the trace upward to green documents (Steps 3–4). A green arrow reads 'Safety Recovery in Few Steps' and points to green badges: 'Recovered Safe Response' and 'Preserved Reasoning Utility'. Panel (b) is a grouped bar chart of Safety Score (blue) and Reasoning Score (pink) for Base MLRM, Reasoning MLRM and Reasoning MLRM + SafeThink (Ours). Teal arrows mark 'Reasoning Fine-tuning' and 'Safety Steering'. An orange callout labeled 'Reasoning Tax' points to the drop in safety.
caption: Overview of SafeThink. (a) Without intervention, reasoning MLRMs process adversarial queries through unsafe reasoning chains, producing harmful responses. SafeThink monitors the reasoning trace and injects a safety steering token when the safety threshold is violated. Safety recovery typically occurs within the first few reasoning steps, after which generation proceeds toward safe completions while preserving reasoning utility. (b) Reasoning fine-tuning improves task performance but degrades safety alignment, resulting in a higher attack success rate (ASR). For example, on the Hades benchmark (Li et al., 2024), R1-Onevision (Yang et al., 2025) exhibits a sharp decline in safety score (defined as 100 −ASR) from 80.87% to 30.93% compared to its base model Qwen2.5-VL, illustrating the reasoning tax on safety. SafeThink recovers safety at inference time without sacrificing reasoning capabilities (Reasoning MLRM + SafeThink).
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) based post-training for explicit chain-of-thought (e.g., GRPO) improves the reasoning ability of multimodal large-scale reasoning models (MLRMs). But recent evidence shows that it can simultaneously degrade safety alignment and increase jailbreak success rates. We propose SafeThink, a lightweight inference-time defense that treats safety recovery as a satisficing constraint rather than a maximization objective. SafeThink monitors the evolving reasoning trace with a safety reward model and conditionally injects an optimized short corrective prefix ("Wait, think safely") only when the safety threshold is violated. In our evaluations across six open-source MLRMs and four jailbreak benchmarks (JailbreakV-28K, Hades, FigStep, and MM-SafetyBench), SafeThink reduces attack success rates by 30-60% (e.g., LlamaV-o1: 63.33% to 5.74% on JailbreakV-28K, R1-Onevision: 69.07% to 5.65% on Hades) while preserving reasoning performance (MathVista accuracy: 65.20% to 65.00%). A key empirical finding from our experiments is that safety recovery is often only a few steering steps away: intervening in the first 1-3 reasoning steps typically suffices to redirect the full generation toward safe completions.
